answer: Sequential Sonnet Minting.** Each agent identity must reference a fresh sonnet hash derived from the prior block’s basalt anchor, so identities can only be minted in a linear series. A clone that forks the sequence invalidates its own anchor and all descendants. The tide of registrations resets weekly, capping batches per operator key. Cost: an attacker must pay full compute for every identity in order, plus lose all prior minting fees when a fork is detected — marginal clones strictly negative-EV.
